section.title: Overview
section.para: On disk, /overlayer holds the layers side by side. The tree below shows a system whose primary C library is musl; shows the same tree with glibc as the primary C library.
section.programlisting: /overlayer/ ├── syshub/ system layer: the base operating system │ ├── bin/ sbin/ libexec/ programs │ ├── lib/ shared libraries of the primary C library │ ├── include/ headers for the libraries in lib/ │ ├── share/ architecture-independent data │ ├── etc/ system configuration │ ├── var/ variable state of base services │ ├── arch-vendor-linux-musl/ primary C library: loader, libc, headers, toolchain │ └── drivers/ │ ├── modules/kernel/ kernel modules │ └── hardware/firmwares/ device firmware ├── userland/ userland layer: software the user installs │ ├── union/ files of installed packages │ │ └── arch-vendor-linux-gnu/ secondary C library, when installed here │ ├── work/ OverlayFS work directory │ ├── registry/ package receipts, index, caches, keys │ └── var/ package data kept outside the union ├── ignition/ ignition layer (read-only) │ ├── kernel/ kernels and initramfs images │ └── bootloader/ boot loader files ├── agents/ instructions for AI agents (optional) └── .syshub-pending/ a staged base upgrade (only while one waits)
section.para: In the running system /overlayer/syshub is the composed view of the system and userland layers (); the other entries are visible at their own paths.

section.title: Layer names
section.para: The names syshub, userland and ignition are the standard names of the three layers, and .syshub-pending the standard name of the staging directory. An implementation SHOULD use them. An implementation MAY give the layers names of its own; it then MUST keep the structure defined here unchanged inside each layer, and MUST document its names in /overlayer (). Everything else in this standard — the root directory, the directories inside each layer, the C library directories and the rules — is the same whatever the layers are called.

section.title: /overlayer/syshub: the system layer
section.para: The system layer is the base operating system as the distribution ships it: C library, toolchain, init system, services, desktop and drivers. It MUST boot and run with the userland layer absent. It MUST be changed only by a base upgrade ().

listitem.para: Programs. sbin holds programs meant for the administrator. Both are on the default PATH.
Helper programs run by other programs, not by users.

Shared and static libraries built for the primary C library, and the data directories that FHS places under /usr/lib (for example lib/systemd, lib/udev, lib/pkgconfig). A library built for any other C library MUST NOT be placed here.
Headers for the libraries in lib. The C library's own headers are in its triplet directory, not here.
Architecture-independent data: icons, locales, manual pages, desktop files, schemas.
System configuration, including the user and group databases, name service, host names and the time zone link. Every C library on the system MUST read these files from here ().
Variable data of base services: logs, caches, spool, the state of the service manager. /var points here.
The primary C library with its loader, headers and cross-named toolchain, and the secondary C library if the distribution ships it in the base ().
Kernel modules of each installed kernel (FHS: /lib/modules).

section.para: The list of base packages and the package mirrors are kept in a directory of the system layer chosen by the implementation.

note.title: Implementation note
note.para: Zainium OS keeps them in /overlayer/syshub/engine/services (syshub.toml, zex_services.toml).

section.title: /overlayer/userland: the userland layer
section.para: The userland layer holds everything the user installs on top of the base. It is changed only by the package manager.

listitem.para: The files of installed packages, in the same layout as the system layer (bin, lib, etc, share, …). This directory is the upper layer of the system view, so its files appear in /overlayer/syshub. A secondary C library installed as a package lives in its triplet directory here ().
The OverlayFS work directory belonging to union. It MUST be on the same filesystem as union and MUST NOT be used for anything else.
One receipt per installed package listing every file it installed, the package index, download caches and trusted signing keys.
Package data that must stay outside the composed view, for example a system-wide Flatpak installation.

section.title: /overlayer/ignition: the ignition layer
section.para: The ignition layer holds what is needed before the root is mounted: kernels, initramfs images and the boot loader (FHS: /boot). It is mounted read-only in the running system. On firmware that can read only FAT filesystems, the installer MAY copy the kernel and initramfs to the EFI system partition; the copies in the ignition layer remain the reference.
An optional directory with instructions, skills and policies for AI coding agents working on the system. Agents SHOULD read it before changing the system.

A base upgrade that has been downloaded and verified but not yet applied. It exists only while an upgrade waits for the next boot, is writable only by the package manager running as root, and MUST be applied or discarded before the system view is composed.

section.title: Documentation at the top of the hierarchy
section.para: An implementation SHOULD place a short description of the system, its architecture, its layer names and its package manager directly in /overlayer, so that the layout explains itself to users and agents.
